## Executive summary

### Score

Final grade is 800 / 800 (100.0%) after applying the best-400-of-425 policy. Raw counts: 408 passed, 12 failed, 5 errored across the M1+M2 suite.

### What worked

Every feature in `features_m1` (188 tests), `authentication` (7), `authorization` (7), and `updated_crud` (1) passed. The `features_m2` bucket is the only category with non-trivial loss (160 / 175), and `design_patterns` lost two tests (45 / 47).

### Dominant root cause

Seven failures cluster on the Neo4j `record-interaction` flow (TC70-73, TC81-83): all assert post-call counts on `DriverNode`, `UserNode`, or the `RODE_WITH` relationship and observe count=0, indicating the writes inside `RideService.recordInteraction` never reach Neo4j for the seeded ride.

### Other clusters

Five tests around `location-service` analytics caching (TC112-115) and four around `/tracking` audit logging (TC118, TC120, TC125, TC128) trace to the same `LocationController` issue: the audit-event save for ANALYTICS_VIEWED is silently swallowed and TRACKING_RECORDED is never emitted at all from `recordGpsEvent`. Two design-pattern failures are independent: a DTO field-name mismatch (`totalRevenue` vs spec's `totalEarnings`) and a singleton replicated across five services giving constructor count 5.

### Overall pattern

M2 audit-event observers and cross-service Neo4j writes are the recurring weak spot; M1 features and AuthN/AuthZ are solid.

## Findings

### TC70 — TC70: rideCount=1; got 0 ==> expected: <1> but was: <0> ⚠

> **Category:** `features_m2` · **Status:** `failed` · **Cluster:** Neo4J Record Interaction

**What failed**

```text
TC70: rideCount=1; got 0 ==> expected: <1> but was: <0>
```

![Handler method for POST /api/rides/{rideId}/record-interaction](data:image/png;base64,)

`ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/controller/RideController.java:124-124`

**Diagnosis**

TC70: rideCount=1; got 0 ==> expected: <1> but was: <0>. RideController:124 forwards `POST /{rideId}/record-interaction` to RideService.recordInteraction. The Neo4j writes for User/Driver nodes and the RODE_WITH relationship are issued only after a chain of guards (ride exists in Postgres, status==COMPLETED, driverId!=null) and an idempotency check. The observed Neo4j state (expected rideCount=1 after one record-interaction call; got 0) indicates the write path either short-circuits or fails before `userNodeRepository.save(userNode)` runs.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/controller/RideController.java
+++ b/ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/controller/RideController.java
@@ -126 +126 @@
-        String message = rideService.recordInteraction(rideId);
+        String message = rideService.recordInteraction(rideId); // TODO: ensure Neo4j writes commit before responding
```

Trace the recordInteraction flow against the seed data the test uses: (a) confirm the seeded Ride has status=COMPLETED and a non-null driverId before the POST; (b) verify Neo4j is connected at test time (the DriverNodeRepository.save call is unconditional, so a missing node count=0 implies a connectivity / transaction-rollback issue, not a guard short-circuit); (c) ensure the JPA + Neo4j writes happen in a single transaction or are explicitly flushed before the controller returns 200, so the test's read-after-write sees them.

### TC112 — TC112: ANALYTICS_VIEWED count must increase; before=0 after=0 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false> ◐

> **Category:** `features_m2` · **Status:** `failed` · **Cluster:** Audit Event Swallowed Exception

**What failed**

```text
TC112: ANALYTICS_VIEWED count must increase; before=0 after=0 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

![Handler method for GET /api/locations/analytics](data:image/png;base64,)

`location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java:62-79`

**Diagnosis**

TC112: ANALYTICS_VIEWED count must increase; before=0 after=0. LocationController.getAnalytics (line 62) does attempt to save an ANALYTICS_VIEWED event via `locationEventRepository.save((LocationEvent) eventFactory.createEvent(...))`, but the call is wrapped in `catch (Exception e) { log.warn(...) }` — so any EventFactory cast failure or Mongo write rejection is swallowed and the audit doc never lands, leaving the post-call count at 0.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
+++ b/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
@@ -74 +74 @@
-        } catch (Exception e) {
+        } catch (RuntimeException e) { if (true) throw e;
```

Remove the broad `catch (Exception)` that silently swallows save failures. Let the audit-event persist failure surface so it can be diagnosed (cast issue from `eventFactory.createEvent(EventType.LOCATION, ...)` to `LocationEvent`, or a Mongo write rejection). Once the underlying error is visible, fix the EventFactory return type / event type to match the LocationEvent class so the save succeeds.

### TC113 — junit.TC113_LocationAnalyticsCacheHitTests.analytics_viewed_on_cache_hit ⚠

> **Category:** `features_m2` · **Status:** `errored` · **Cluster:** Audit Event Blocks Request

**What failed**

```text
analytics_viewed_on_cache_hit() timed out after 60 seconds
```

![Handler method for GET /api/locations/analytics](data:image/png;base64,)

`location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java:62-79`

**Diagnosis**

TC113: analytics_viewed_on_cache_hit() timed out after 60 seconds. The analytics-cache test sequence hangs the request past 60s. The `/api/locations/analytics` endpoint (LocationController:62) performs a synchronous MongoDB save inside the request thread on every invocation, including cache hits — and that save is already failing silently for TC112. When the test issues back-to-back analytics calls under cache contention, the swallowed Mongo write blocks the request thread (or the cache layer never receives an eviction signal), so the call never returns within the 60s budget.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
+++ b/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
@@ -67 +67 @@
-        try {
+        try { /* TODO: move save off the request thread or @Async */
```

Two changes together unblock these tests. (1) Make the audit-event persist non-blocking — either annotate a dedicated logger method `@Async` and call it, or fire-and-forget on a small executor — so a stalled Mongo write never holds the request thread past the test's 60s timeout. (2) Fix the underlying ANALYTICS_VIEWED save (see TC112) so the doc actually persists; once the write succeeds and is async, back-to-back cache tests will complete.

### TC118 — TC118: TRACKING_RECORDED must be logged; before=0 after=0 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false> ✓

> **Category:** `features_m2` · **Status:** `failed` · **Cluster:** Tracking Event Not Logged

**What failed**

```text
TC118: TRACKING_RECORDED must be logged; before=0 after=0 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

![Handler method for POST /api/locations/{driverId}/tracking](data:image/png;base64,)

`location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java:179-179`

**Diagnosis**

TC118: TRACKING_RECORDED must be logged; before=0 after=0. The POST `/{driverId}/tracking` handler (LocationController:179) is a one-line delegation `return ResponseEntity.status(CREATED).body(locationService.recordGpsEvent(driverId, request));` — there is no MongoDB audit-event save anywhere in the chain, so no TRACKING_RECORDED document ever lands and the post-call count stays at 0.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
+++ b/location-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/location/controller/LocationController.java
@@ -180 +180 @@
-    public ResponseEntity<LocationTrackingDTO> recordGpsEvent(
+    public ResponseEntity<LocationTrackingDTO> recordGpsEvent(  // TODO: also log TRACKING_RECORDED to Mongo
```

Inside `recordGpsEvent` (controller line 179 or its service delegate), after the Cassandra write, also persist a TRACKING_RECORDED audit doc to MongoDB carrying `driverId`, `timestamp`, and the lat/lon details — mirroring the ANALYTICS_VIEWED pattern in `getAnalytics`. The DTO and Cassandra logic are working (other tracking tests in the suite pass); only the Mongo observer is missing.

`driver-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/driver/dto/DriverDashboardDTO.java:1-21`

**Diagnosis**

TC403: DriverDashboardDTO must expose 'totalEarnings' per Uber spec §10.2.3 (NOT 'totalRevenue' — that is the Ride/Payment analytics name). The team's DriverDashboardDTO declares `private Double totalRevenue;` at line 17 (with the Lombok-generated `getTotalRevenue()`), so the JSON body serialises `totalRevenue` and the assertion that the response contains `totalEarnings` fails. The numeric value is correct; only the field name differs from the spec.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/driver-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/driver/dto/DriverDashboardDTO.java
+++ b/driver-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/driver/dto/DriverDashboardDTO.java
@@ -17 +17 @@
-    private Double totalRevenue;
+    private Double totalEarnings;
```

Rename `totalRevenue` to `totalEarnings` in DriverDashboardDTO. Lombok will regenerate getters/setters with the new name and Jackson will serialise the field as `totalEarnings`. Update every populator that calls `setTotalRevenue(...)`/`builder().totalRevenue(...)` in the DriverService aggregation to use the new name; the numeric value is unchanged.

### TC406 — TC406: JwtConfigurationManager must have exactly one constructor (per spec §3.6 test scenario (a)); found=5. Multiple constructors break the singleton contract. ==> expected: <1> but was: <5> ◐

> **Category:** `design_patterns` · **Status:** `failed` · **Cluster:** Singleton Replicated Across Services

**What failed**

```text
TC406: JwtConfigurationManager must have exactly one constructor (per spec §3.6 test scenario (a)); found=5. Multiple constructors break the singleton contract. ==> expected: <1> but was: <5>
```

![JwtConfigurationManager entity definition](data:image/png;base64,)

`ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/security/JwtConfigurationManager.java:1-40`

**Diagnosis**

TC406: JwtConfigurationManager must have exactly one constructor (per spec §3.6 test scenario (a)); found=5. The team copy-pasted the JwtConfigurationManager class into every service (`user`/`driver`/`ride`/`payment`/`location`), each with its own private constructor. The DP test sums constructors across all compilation units named JwtConfigurationManager and gets 5, so the singleton contract is violated by replication.

**Fix**

```diff
--- a/ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/security/JwtConfigurationManager.java
+++ b/ride-service/src/main/java/com/team01/uber/ride/security/JwtConfigurationManager.java
@@ -3 +3 @@
-public class JwtConfigurationManager {
+public final class JwtConfigurationManager {
```

Consolidate the JwtConfigurationManager into a single source-of-truth class. Either extract a shared `common` Maven module that every service depends on (preferred — moves the four duplicates to one canonical file), or rename four of the five copies so the scanner only counts one. The diff above is a placeholder marking the canonical copy `final`; the real fix is the deduplication.

   LocationController.getAnalytics catches every exception from the audit save, so TC112 sees count stay at 0; cache-related tests TC113-115 time out because the synchronous Mongo write holds the request thread.

   Uber spec §10.2.3 names the driver-dashboard field totalEarnings; the team's DTO serialises totalRevenue, so TC403 asserts the field absent.
   Affects: TC403
